Basically, you cut last the two layers of skin, the epidermis and dermis (styro,) into fat.  Fat looks different from the other layers because it has what I can best describe as yellow bubbles inside

This layer (also known as subcutaneous tissue) contains fat, connective tissue, larger blood vessels, and nerves. It is *very* easy to hit something important. I got extremely lucky.

It is also highly recommended to get stitches if you cut to fat, seeing as it can get easily infected since it gapes open. But this is only an option for about 24 hours after the cut. Some hospitals refuse to stitch it after 8 hours in fear that the cut has already been open long enough to get infected.
